title: Every day the best day
hook: write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year (Society and Solitude)
tomorrow: hitch your wagon to a star

segments.voice: Yesterday, Brahma: Emerson's poem drawing on the Gita and the Upanishads. Your line was he read the east. What line from another tradition did you sit with? Day one thousand two hundred nine.

Friday. Payday. The trip in the spring. The day the project ships, the day the kids are older, the day things finally calm down. A good share of a life can be spent leaning toward some other day, the one where living will properly begin. Emerson has a short essay in his book Society and Solitude called Works and Days, and in it he says something that sounds like a greeting card until you try to actually do it. Today, his claim about which day is the best one.
screen: `FRIDAY. PAYDAY. THE TRIP.` → `LEANING TOWARD ANOTHER DAY.` → `WHICH DAY IS THE BEST?`

segments.voice: First, the line. In Works and Days, Emerson writes: "Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year." Not the best day of the week. The best in the year. Every one of them. On its face it sounds impossible. Second, what he means by owning a day. In the same essay he says, "He only is rich who owns the day," and that nobody owns a day if they let it be overrun by fret and worry. So the best day isn't the one where everything goes right. It's the one you actually live in, instead of renting it out to tomorrow's anxieties. Third, his picture of the days. Emerson describes the days coming and going like veiled figures, sent from a friendly party far away. They don't announce themselves. They say nothing. And if we don't use the gifts they bring, they carry them away again just as quietly. That's the edge in his line. A day isn't the best because it's pleasant. It's the best because it's the only one holding its gifts out to you right now. Fourth, what it isn't. It isn't a forced smile on a hard day. A day can be grief and still be the one you have. It can be dull and still be carrying something. Emerson's challenge is to stop treating today as a waiting room. The best day in the year isn't the one circled on the calendar. It's this one, the one with gifts in its hands that will go back out the door unopened if nobody looks.
screen: `WRITE IT ON YOUR HEART.` · `HE ONLY IS RICH WHO OWNS THE DAY.` · `THE DAYS COME VEILED, WITH GIFTS.` · `NOT A FORCED SMILE.` · then, large: `EVERY DAY IS THE BEST DAY IN THE YEAR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: treat today as the best day. Settle, and breathe. Let today so far pass in front of you, without judging it: waking up, the first light, the first conversation. Look for one gift the day has already held out, something small you might have walked past. A kind word, a taste, a moment of quiet. Then look ahead to the hours left, and wonder what this day might still be carrying that you haven't unwrapped yet. The bell holds the time.
Every day the best day. Emerson's line from Works and Days: write it on your heart, because today is the day holding its gifts out. Today's word.
screen: `EVERY DAY THE BEST DAY — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the best day. When you catch yourself waiting for some later day today, stop, and take one gift this one is offering. Day one thousand two hundred nine.

howItsDone: Readers sometimes copy this line from Emerson's Works and Days onto a card or the first page of a journal, as a daily reminder to live the present day rather than wait for a better one.
